title: Delta-driven promptset signature and access protocol
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Configuration changes (model switches, quantization profiles, runtime flags) can silently degrade output quality when paired with uncurated prompt sets. We need an automated, low-latency way to detect meaningful changes to our canonical/golden prompt bundles and tie those deltas to eval runs and gating logic.

Proposal: Implement a promptset registry that records immutable snapshots with a deterministic fingerprint and a steward signature. On config or model changes, the system computes a delta between the currently pinned snapshot and the most-recently-evaluated snapshot; if the delta exceeds a threshold (content-level or example-level), it triggers targeted regression evals and creates an action item in the rollout pipeline.

Key capabilities:
- Deterministic fingerprinting: canonicalize prompts (normalize whitespace, strip non-essential metadata, stable ordering by internal ID) then hash (SHA-256) to produce a promptset fingerprint.
- Semantic delta: compute both token-level diff and embedding-based similarity per example (cosine similarity threshold) to catch rewordings that change model behavior.
- Immutable snapshots: store promptsets as content-addressed blobs with metadata (author, steward, creation_time, signed_by). Snapshots are immutable; updates create a new snapshot.
- Steward signature & ACLs: require a steward signature (ECDSA with KMS-backed keys) for a snapshot to be considered 'trusted gold'. ACLs control who can create, approve, or mark snapshots as trusted. All access and approval events are auditable.
- CI and rollout integration: on PRs that change config or model pins, compute delta against the pinned trusted snapshot and attach a recommended eval suite. If delta>threshold, block merge or escalate to canary run depending on policy.

Why different from existing work: This ticket focuses on the signing/access protocol and the delta-driven triggers rather than curation UX or dataset UI. It defines the canonicalization/signing primitives and the event hooks that wire into CI, the console, and the eval runner.
acceptance_criteria: Registry stores immutable promptset snapshots with deterministic SHA-256 fingerprints
Snapshots can be signed using KMS-backed steward keys; signature verifiable via the registry API
Delta computation produces a numeric score and classification (none, minor, major) and is exposed in API and PR checks
Policy engine uses delta classification to decide: no action, run targeted eval suite, or block rollout
Audit logs show who created, signed, and accessed trusted snapshots for at least 90 days
E2E test: simulate a model/config change and observe expected eval trigger and CI gate behavior

notes: Trade-offs: strict signing increases friction for small edits; we'll allow ‘draft’ snapshots that are unsigned for iterating, with explicit promotion to trusted snapshots.
Storage: content-addressed blobs reduce duplicated storage across snapshots but require GC policy for old bundles — propose 180-day hot retention, archive thereafter.
False positives: embedding thresholds will be calibrated per-bundle; include a human-in-the-loop label override for edge cases.
Privacy: promptsets may contain PII; ensure encryption-at-rest and access controls mirror private deployment requirements.
